correction.text: Attica and Laconia, the two Greek members; hatched over the Antigonid vassal tint for Attica (rule 5)

keyframe_review.note: 10.8 k km2, Attica and Laconia, dated 264-257 by Cliopatria. The war's infobox is '267-261 BC' ('possibly as early as the autumn of 268 BC'), Athens surrendered 'in either 262 BC or 261 BC': re-date to 267-261. The extent matches the page's belligerents (Athens, Sparta, the Ptolemaic Kingdom); the decree's further members (Elis, the Achaeans, Tegea, Mantinea, Orchomenus, Phigalia) are 'not mentioned' on the page opened and are left out at this confidence. The Ptolemaic fleet's base at Koroni in Attica is inside the shape.

ledger.note: 267 (or autumn 268): 'the anti-Macedonian faction under Chremonides' took power in Athens and 'declared war' on Antigonus Gonatas, allied with Areus I of Sparta and Ptolemy II. Infobox 'Date 267-261 BC'.

267-261: rule 6 blend over Attica and the Isthmus, where Areus tried to break through to Athens. The antigonid-dynasty dossier carries the matching pair. 'After the indecisive campaign season of 266 BC' a Ptolemaic fleet under Patroclus aided Athens.
262/261: Athens 'starved into surrender in either 262 BC or 261 BC'. Dated 261 with the infobox.

261: the war 'confirmed Antigonid control over Greece'; Athens 'lost her last pre-Hellenistic vestiges of political independence'. The Ptolemaic fleet was beaten at Cos 'probably in 261 BC'. [Reviewer eu-02-a, 2026-10-18: counterpart antigonid-dynasty to greek-city-states: Athens returns to the Greek city-states row under the Antigonid vassal tint (antigonid-dynasty /ledger/22, greek-city-states /ledger/59); the 265 'loss' of a Corinth radius the alliance never held was deleted, the contest pair covers Areus's defeat.]
261: 'Macedonian victory' (infobox). Sparta returns to the Greek city-state colour; Athens to the Antigonid tint. Cliopatria's shape runs to 257.

wars.name: Chremonidean War

zones.text: the siege of Athens; Patroclus's base

wars.outcome: 'Macedonian victory': Athens surrendered (262/261), Areus I killed (265), the Ptolemaic fleet beaten at Cos; 'Antigonid control over Greece' confirmed.

certainty.note: Two city-states and a fleet: the hatch covers their home territories, not a frontier.

notes: Split from Cliopatria's 'Athenian Coalition' row, whose second shape (264-257, Attica and Laconia) is the Chremonidean War alliance, unrelated to the Lamian War coalition of 323-322 that the first shape shows (dossier athenian-coalition). Wikidata Q1073686 is the Chremonidean War item as best known to the researcher; not verifiable here (wikidata.org unreachable) and to be checked by the reviewer. Typed rebel: Athens's revolt against Antigonid hegemony, to be hatched over the Antigonid tint (rule 5); Sparta's part may equally be drawn in the Greek city-state colour. Re-dated 267-261. Members named in the decree of Chremonides beyond Athens and Sparta are not on the page opened and are left for a gap-filler ('Chremonides').
